### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 66)

USF wound up being a good stop for a promising, up-and- coming, offensive mind with his first head coaching job in Alex Golesh. Golesh has now leveled up to Auburn after posting a trio of winning seasons in Tampa. Now it’s Brian Hartline’s turn, as the world’s best wide receiver recruiter has left Ohio State to put his stamp on his own program. Hartline hasn’t coached anywhere other than Columbus in his collegiate career, so we’ll see how it goes, but his first objective will be to try and keep up the offensive standards set by Golesh. Five teams averaged 40+ PPG last season and the Bulls were one of them. In American Conference play, the Bulls averaged 49 PPG. That’s a high bar to live up to, but what really established the ceiling for USF was that the defense improved at a similar pace to the offense. With basically a brand-new roster and his first try as a head coach, Hartline has his work cut out for him this season. Under 8.5 With over 4,000 yards and 42 touchdowns from Byrum Brown, USF went 9-3 in the regular season last year. While the non-conference slate is substantially easier this time around, the Bulls play Memphis and UTSA on short weeks, with Memphis coming off of the bye for that game. From a spread standpoint, USF could be favored in 10 or 11 games, but there’s a reason why the vig is slanting towards the Under and why a lot of questions without answers have the market down on this program this season. My projection is 8.56 wins.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 67)*, with the answers as written:

### Hype or hope?

Not all highly-touted recruits make it. The transfer portal gives players with that kind of pedigree the chance to go to a G6 program and attempt to get back on the radar. At USF, most of those players are quarterbacks, as Hartline and OC Tim Beck got Michael Van Buren by way of Mississippi State and LSU and Luke Kromenhoek by way of Florida State and Mississippi State. MVB did have some success at those two stops, including an 8/2 TD/INT ratio at LSU last season with four starts and some relief efforts. There are so many unproven players on this side of the ball and it’s fair to wonder if Hartline is a program-builder or was just able to thrive with the foundation already set at Ohio State.

### What the Beck?

You can understand why Hartline turned to Tim Beck as the OC, as the 60-year-old has been coaching since the late ‘80s. It took him 35 years to get his first head coaching gig and it didn’t go particularly well at Coastal Carolina with a 20-18 record. So, he’s an OC again and I find it underwhelming, personally. Most of the guys acquired via free agency didn’t play very much at their previous schools, but 247Sports graded USF’s portal haul the best in the conference and 58th nationally with 44 total commits. That’s a lot of scouting and a lot of new faces.

### Could the defense outpace the offense in 2026?

While the hiring of Beck is pretty bland in my eyes, the hiring of Josh Aldridge as DC is not. Aldridge has been working at conference rival East Carolina under head coach Blake Harrell, who has proven to be an outstanding defensive mind and a pretty darn good HC. Stopping the run is the key to success in this conference. Most teams run the ball well or have run-heavy schemes. Aldridge’s ECU unit allowed just 3.6 yards per carry. Everybody seems to allow passing yards and 60+% completion percentages, but the teams that stop the run position themselves for success. That was true of USF last season with just 3.7 YPC. This may not be a polished defense, but it is a big front seven.
